levelledPara.title: Purpose
levelledPara.para: The Illustrated Part Data (IPD) includes all parts of the component(s) shown on the title page that can be disassembled, repaired or replaced, and reassembled.

Each assembly is recorded and immediately followed by a record of its detail parts. The record is indentured to show the difference between each part and the higher assembly. Item numbers in the parts list agree with the item numbers of the included illustration (figure).

The IPD will be used to identify parts and their relationship to each other. It will contain one or more figures depending on complexity or variant assemblies, with exploded views to show all the removable, disassembly and procurable parts or repairable parts.

levelledPara.title: Numerical Index
levelledPara.para: The Alphanumerical Index is an aid to find parts in the Detailed Parts List (DPL) by part number.It gives the Figure Number, the Item Number and the Total quantity Required for each entry.

levelledPara.title: Explanation and Use of Detailed Parts List (DPL)
Indentation System
levelledPara.para: The indentation system used in the parts list shows the relation of the parts to each other. For a given item, the number of indentures shows the relation of the item to the Next Higher Assembly (NHA), as follows:

levelledPara.title: Usable on Code Assembly
levelledPara.para: In IPD figures that have more than one top assembly item, reference letters (A, B, C, etc.) are given to each top assembly item in the USABLE ON CODE ASSEMBLY column. The reference letter of the applicable top assembly is also shown in the USABLE ON CODE ASSEMBLY column for each detail part and subassembly, except that no reference letter is shown for detail parts and subassemblies used on all top assemblies.

levelledPara.title: Unit per assy
levelledPara.para: The UNIT PER ASSY column shows the total number of units required per assembly, per subassembly, and per sub-subassembly as applicable. For bulk items, the abbreviation AR is used for "as required". The abbreviation RF shows the item is listed for reference purposes. The abbreviation NP is used for a part if it is not procurable.

The abbreviation “NP” besides the quantity shows the item is "NOT PROCURABLE". The abbreviation “RPD” besides the quantity shows the item is "REPLACED". The abbreviation “SPD” besides the quantity shows the item is "SUPERSEDED", the abbreviation “BFE” besides the quantity shows the item is “BFE”.

levelledPara.para: The interchangeability relationship between parts is identified in the DESCRIPTION column of the parts list. A list of the terms used to show interchangeability and their definition is as follows:

The part in the part number column is superseded by and is not interchangeable with the item number shown in the notation.
The part in the part number column supersedes and is not interchangeable with the item number shown in the notation.

levelledPara.title: Items not Illustrated
levelledPara.para: Items not illustrated are shown by a dash (-) in front of the item number in the ITEM column.

levelledPara.title: Abbreviations and Terminology Used in Description Column

listItem.para: ORDER OVRLGTH MPN XXXXXXXXXX: Identifies a part number with more than fifteen characters that cannot fit in the part number column.

SB XX-XXX: Identifies the Service Bulletin (SB) which adds to or changes the Detailed Parts List. When the SB number shown in the name column is related to an AIRWORTHINESS DIRECTIVE (AD), the letters AD and its number are shown in parenthesis. Also they will follow the SB number, for example: PRE SB XX XXX (AD XXXX), POST SB XX XXX (AD XXXX), ADDED by SB XX XXX (AD XXXX), DELETED BY SB XX XXX (AD XXX), etc.
SEL FROM: Identifies a group of alternative parts from which you can take the necessary ones.
OPT TO: Identifies an optional part that is fully interchangeable with the initial part.
ALT: Identifies an alternate part number that is fully interchangeable with the initial part.
NP: Identifies an item that is not supplied (Not Procurable).

USED ON PN: Identifies the NHA for a part in the part number column. This is used when the NHA is not clear from the Usage Code (almost the same assemblies with details that are not the same but have a single breakdown).
See for DET / See For NHA: See XX-XX-XX-XX for DET or NHA gives the location in the IPL of either a full breakdown or the NHA of a sub-assembly.
RPLS XXX = replaces part number. RPLD BY XXX = replaced by part number.

levelledPara.title: How to find a part with a known part number
levelledPara.para: When the part number is known, find the part number in the Numerical index. Record the figure and item number. Find the item number in the applicable parts list and illustration to get the necessary data.

levelledPara.title: How to find a part and its number when only the assembly part number is known
levelledPara.para: When the part number is not known, look at the illustrations to identify the part by shape and location. Refer to the included parts list to get the PART NUMBER, DESCRIPTION, EFFECTIVITY, and QUANTITY.

levelledPara.title: Addition of Color Code into Part Number

levelledPara.para: Integration of color code into part number
To include the color information into the part number, the dashes have been removed and color code added at the end of the part number.
Example: P/N 50-000610-024-0 with color code H022 Becomes 500006100240022

note.notePara: These part numbers are two ways interchangeable.

levelledPara.para: The new codification has been introduced in all CMM initial release or revision issued after June 10th 2005 (See example ).
Addition of Supplier Number (REF) in the CMM

Each Safran Seats France part has a Supplier Number indicated on its identification label (See ). This REF number has been added as additional information in the "1234567 nomenclature" column of the CMM (See ).
It is recommended to the customer to add this Supplier Number (REF) in the purchase order to improve delay and reliability in spare part data processing.
